reason: Broken on the wording, on the two points the evidence claimed to have checked. I downloaded the Jolas scan the evidence names (archive.org item G.BachelardThePoeticsOfSpace, the djvu text, 563,847 bytes) and read the paragraph. It runs: 'This being the case, if I were asked to name the chief / benefit of the house, I should say: the house shelters day¬ / dreaming, the house protects the dreamer, the house allows / one to dream in peace. Thought and experience are not / the only things that sanction human values. The values / that belong to daydreaming mark humanity in its depths. / Daydreaming even has a privilege of autovalorization.' FIRST DEFECT: the sentence does not begin 'If I were asked'. It begins 'This being the case, if I were asked'. The proposal silently drops the opening clause and raises the lower-case 'if' to a capital 'If', which is minted wording: that exact sentence, so capitalised, exists in no edition. It is the rendering that circulates on quotation sites, which is where it looks to have come from. SECOND DEFECT: 'day-dreaming' is not a hyphen in Bachelard, it is the scan's end-of-line break hyphen, printed in this OCR as '¬' at the end of the line ('shelters day¬' / 'dreaming'). The paragraph's own spelling is solid: the next two sentences read 'daydreaming' and 'Daydreaming', and the sentence after that 'daydream'. Across the whole file the solid forms appear 170 times against 10 genuinely hyphenated ones, and 13 further '¬' line-breaks. The evidence asserts 'it reads day-dreaming with a hyphen, exactly as the proposal has it' and that is exactly the trap: a line-break hyphen read as a real one. What survives: the locator is right. The running heads put the page-5 head at the paragraph above and the page-7 head just below, so the passage is on p. 6, in ch. 1, 'The House. From Cellar to Garret. The Significance of the Hut', and the title page of the scan is the Jolas translation, Orion Press 1964, from La poetique de l'espace, PUF 1958, reprinted by Beacon. shipped.js: no match, Bachelard at 0 of 3, not banned. So the citation is salvageable, but not this quotation as written.
betterCitation: Ship it only in the Jolas wording: “This being the case, if I were asked to name the chief benefit of the house, I should say: the house shelters daydreaming, the house protects the dreamer, the house allows one to dream in peace.” Source line: Gaston Bachelard, The Poetics of Space, ch. 1, ‘The House. From Cellar to Garret’, p. 6 (trans. Maria Jolas, 1964)
